symbols.name: \mathcal G
symbols.space: An acyclic directed mixed graph on \(V\cup\{S\}\).

symbols.name: W_\star
symbols.role: baseline vertex in the first exact audit gate

symbols.name: A_\star
symbols.role: treatment vertex in the first exact audit gate

symbols.name: Y_\star
symbols.role: outcome vertex in the first exact audit gate

symbols.name: \mathcal G_\star
symbols.def: The graph on \(\{W_\star,A_\star,Y_\star,S\}\) with directed edges \(W_\star\to A_\star\), \(W_\star\to Y_\star\), \(W_\star\to S\), \(A_\star\to Y_\star\), and \(Y_\star\to S\), and bidirected edge \(Y_\star\leftrightarrow S\).

symbols.name: T_0
symbols.role: variables with an unbiased joint margin

symbols.name: A
symbols.role: random-variable block of a canonical kernel key

symbols.name: B
symbols.role: intervention block of a canonical kernel key

symbols.name: C
symbols.role: ordinary conditioning block of a canonical kernel key

symbols.name: H
symbols.role: finite block moved by a transition

symbols.name: S_s
symbols.def: \(S_{\mathrm{pop}}=\varnothing\) and \(S_{\mathrm{sel}}=\{S\}\).

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: \(\kappa=(A,B,C,s)\) with \(A,B,C\) pairwise disjoint and \(A\ne\varnothing\).

symbols.name: \mathcal X_A
symbols.def: For every \(A\subseteq V\), \(\mathcal X_A=\prod_{W\in A}\mathcal X_W\).

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: \(r=\max_{W\in V}\lvert\mathcal X_W\rvert\).

symbols.name: \xi
symbols.def: \(\xi=(A,B,C,s,a,b,c)\), where \(\kappa=(A,B,C,s)\) is a table-level key and \(a\in\mathcal X_A\), \(b\in\mathcal X_B\), and \(c\in\mathcal X_C\); the unique cell of an empty block is denoted by \(\ast\).

symbols.name: q_S
symbols.def: \(q_S(v)=P(V=v\mid S=1)\).

symbols.name: q_S^M
symbols.def: \(q_S^M(v)=P_M(V=v\mid S=1)\), defined when \(P_M(S=1)>0\).
symbols.role: selected law induced by a model

symbols.name: q_0^M
symbols.role: unbiased margin induced by a model

symbols.name: k_\kappa
symbols.type: kernel table named by a canonical key
symbols.def: For \(\kappa=(A,B,C,s)\), \(k_\kappa^M(a\mid b,c)=P_M(A=a\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,S_s)\), where the last argument is absent for \(s=\mathrm{pop}\) and is \(S=1\) for \(s=\mathrm{sel}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal R
symbols.def: A collection of deterministic response maps and a product law on finitely supported independent exogenous coordinates that induces \(M\), with the declared state space of every exogenous coordinate defined to be exactly its positive-probability support; zero-mass labels are not coordinates of the representation.
symbols.role: representation held fixed by the projective perturbation

symbols.name: \mathbf U
symbols.type: finite vector of independent exogenous response coordinates
symbols.def: The exogenous coordinates and their product law in \(\mathcal R\); for each coordinate, its finite state space is exactly the set of atoms assigned strictly positive mass.

symbols.name: U_0
symbols.def: One coordinate of \(\mathbf U\) in the fixed representation \(\mathcal R\).
symbols.role: only exogenous coordinate whose atom masses are perturbed

symbols.name: \mathcal J_0
symbols.def: \(\mathcal J_0=\{\omega:P_{\mathcal R}(U_0=\omega)>0\}\), and this finite set is the declared state space of \(U_0\).

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: \(m=\lvert\mathcal J_0\rvert\).
symbols.role: number of active atoms of the perturbed exogenous variable

symbols.name: \mathfrak M_{\epsilon}
symbols.def: Compatible models with \(P_M(S=1)>0\) and model-induced selected cells \(q_S^M(v)\ge\epsilon\) for every \(v\).

symbols.name: \operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M)=(q_S^M,q_0^M)=(P_M(V\mid S=1),P_M(T_0))\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C_{\epsilon}
symbols.def: \(\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)=\{\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M):M\in\mathfrak M_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G)\}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak F_{\epsilon}
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)=\{M\in\mathfrak M_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G):\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M)=(q_S,q_0)\}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak R_{\epsilon,\eta}^{\circ}
symbols.def: Triples \((M,\mathcal R,U_0)\) in which \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\), \(\mathcal R\) is the chosen finite independent response representation whose every coordinate state space is exactly its positive support, and every atom in every such state space has mass at least \(\eta\).

symbols.name: \psi_{x,y}
symbols.def: \(\psi_{x,y}(M)=P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))\).

symbols.name: \mathcal I
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I=\mathcal X_X\times\mathcal X_Y\).

symbols.name: \boldsymbol\psi
symbols.def: \(\boldsymbol\psi(M)=\{\psi_{x,y}(M):(x,y)\in\mathcal I\}=\{P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x)):(x,y)\in\mathcal I\}\).

symbols.name: \theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}
symbols.def: When \(X\) is binary and \(Y\) is numeric, \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(M)=E_M[Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=1)]-E_M[Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0)]\).

symbols.name: u
symbols.def: For every active index \(j\in\mathcal J_0\), \(u_j=P_{\mathcal R}(U_0=j)>0\) in the fixed triple \((M,\mathcal R,U_0)\); there are no coordinates outside \(\mathcal J_0\), and all response maps and all other exogenous-coordinate laws are held fixed.

symbols.name: a_v
symbols.def: For the fixed \((M,\mathcal R,U_0)\) and every \(j\in\mathcal J_0\), \(a_v(j)=P_{\mathcal R}(V=v,S=1\mid U_0=j)\), integrating over the positive-support state spaces of the other coordinates of \(\mathbf U\).

symbols.name: a_+
symbols.def: For every \(j\in\mathcal J_0\), \(a_+(j)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal X_V}a_v(j)=P_{\mathcal R}(S=1\mid U_0=j)\).

symbols.name: b_t
symbols.def: For the fixed \((M,\mathcal R,U_0)\) and every \(j\in\mathcal J_0\), \(b_t(j)=P_{\mathcal R}(T_0=t\mid U_0=j)\), integrating over the positive-support state spaces of the other coordinates of \(\mathbf U\).

symbols.name: h_{x,y}
symbols.def: For the fixed \((M,\mathcal R,U_0)\) and every \(j\in\mathcal J_0\), \(h_{x,y}(j)=P_{\mathcal R}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),U_0=j)\), integrating over the positive-support state spaces of the other coordinates of \(\mathbf U\); no inactive response label indexes this row.

symbols.name: \Gamma_{(M,\mathcal R,U_0)}
symbols.space: a linear subspace of \(\mathbb R^{\mathcal J_0}\cong\mathbb R^m\)

symbols.name: u^{\pm}
symbols.type: pair of perturbed chosen-coordinate mass vectors
symbols.def: \(u^{\pm}_j=u_j\pm\tau\beta_j\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J_0\); no inactive coordinate is added.

symbols.name: \mathcal R_1
symbols.def: When \(u^+\in\Delta(\mathcal J_0)^{\circ}\), the representation obtained from \(\mathcal R\) by assigning \(U_0\) the mass vector \(u^+\) on the unchanged positive-support state space \(\mathcal J_0\) and leaving every response map and other exogenous law unchanged; it induces \(M_1\).

symbols.name: \mathcal R_2
symbols.def: When \(u^-\in\Delta(\mathcal J_0)^{\circ}\), the representation obtained from \(\mathcal R\) by assigning \(U_0\) the mass vector \(u^-\) on the unchanged positive-support state space \(\mathcal J_0\) and leaving every response map and other exogenous law unchanged; it induces \(M_2\).

symbols.name: F_{x,y}
symbols.def: For the fixed input cell \((x,y)\), \(F_{x,y}\) is a scalar expression built from cells of \(q_S,q_0\) by finite sums, products, and divisions by positive denominators.

symbols.name: \mathcal A
symbols.def: The closure of cells of \(q_S,q_0\) under finite sums, products, and divisions by positive denominators.

symbols.name: d
symbols.def: \(d=\lvert\mathcal I\rvert\).

symbols.name: \mathbf F
symbols.def: \(\mathbf F=(F_{x,y}:(x,y)\in\mathcal I)^{\mathsf T}\) in a fixed lexicographic cell order, whenever every cell run returns an arithmetic expression.

symbols.name: \mathscr K_{\mathcal G}
symbols.def: \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}=\{(A,B,C,s,a,b,c):\varnothing\ne A\subseteq V,\ A,B,C\text{ pairwise disjoint},\ s\in\{\mathrm{pop},\mathrm{sel}\},\ a\in\mathcal X_A,\ b\in\mathcal X_B,\ c\in\mathcal X_C\}\). Thus \(\lvert\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\rvert=2\sum_{A\ne\varnothing,\,A,B,C\,\mathrm{disjoint}}\lvert\mathcal X_A\rvert\lvert\mathcal X_B\rvert\lvert\mathcal X_C\rvert\le2\{(1+3r)^{\lvert V\rvert}-(1+2r)^{\lvert V\rvert}\}<2(1+3r)^{\lvert V\rvert}\).
symbols.role: graph-fixed cell identities for scalar normalized interventional-kernel annotations

symbols.name: \mathscr L
symbols.def: \(\mathscr L=(\mathrm{popstore},\mathrm{margin},\mathrm{popfix}_1,\mathrm{popfix}_2,\mathrm{popfix}_3,\mathrm{selfix}_1,\mathrm{selfix}_2,\mathrm{selfix}_3,\mathrm{marginal},\mathrm{condition},\mathrm{chain})\) in the displayed branch order.

symbols.name: \mathscr U
symbols.def: \(\mathscr U\) is the subset of \(\mathscr L\times2^V\times2^{\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}}\times\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\) whose coordinates give the move tag, moved block \(H\), complete finite set of required scalar input keys, and one scalar output key specified by the exact probability, graphical-fixing, or source-bridge transition relation. The order is first by \(\mathscr L\), then by a fixed lexicographic order on subsets, finite input-key sets, and output keys, and \(\lvert\mathscr U\rvert\le11\cdot2^{\lvert V\rvert}2^{\lvert\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\rvert}\lvert\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\rvert\). Arithmetic expressions and derivation lengths are not move-instance coordinates.

symbols.name: \sigma
symbols.def: For the fixed procedure input \((\mathcal G,X,Y,x,y,T_0,q_S,q_0)\), \(\sigma=(K_\sigma,E_\sigma)\), where \(K_\sigma\subseteq\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\) is the finite set of present scalar cell keys and \(E_\sigma\) assigns each present key one scalar arithmetic-expression annotation and one provenance pointer in \(\mathscr U\cup\{\mathrm{init}_S,\mathrm{init}_0\}\); transition eligibility and duplicate detection depend on \(K_\sigma\), not on the spelling of an annotation.

symbols.name: K_\sigma
symbols.def: The first coordinate of \(\sigma\); membership records a canonical scalar cell key, never its arithmetic formula.

symbols.name: E_\sigma
symbols.def: The second coordinate of \(\sigma\), a partial map from scalar keys \(\xi\in\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\) to scalar expressions in \(\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\), paired with a provenance pointer in \(\mathscr U\cup\{\mathrm{init}_S,\mathrm{init}_0\}\); its values do not generate key identities and are ignored by duplicate detection and the termination measure.

symbols.name: \mu
symbols.def: \(\mu(\sigma)=\lvert\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\setminus K_\sigma\rvert\).

symbols.name: \operatorname{QE}_3
symbols.def: A real-closed-field quantifier-elimination and cylindrical-algebraic-decomposition procedure for binary selection ADMGs with at most three substantive vertices. It enumerates only the finite graph, query specification \((T_0,X,Y,x,y)\), and canonical \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}\) branch choices; it keeps \(q_S,q_0,\epsilon\) as free real parameters and returns a finite semialgebraic partition with branchwise validity or exact-fiber witness certificates.

symbols.name: e_o
symbols.def: The coordinate vector equal to one at cell \(o\) and zero elsewhere.

symbols.name: \lambda
symbols.def: \(n_S/n\to\lambda\).

symbols.name: \widehat q_S
symbols.def: \(\widehat q_S(v)=n_S^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_S}\mathbf 1\{O_i^S=v\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat{\mathbf F}
symbols.def: \(\widehat{\mathbf F}=\mathbf F(\widehat q_S,\widehat q_0)\).

symbols.name: D_S\mathbf F
symbols.def: The Fréchet derivative of \(\mathbf F\) in the selected-source multinomial tangent space \(\{z\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal X_V\rvert}:\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}z=0\}\), evaluated at \(q_S\).

symbols.name: D_0\mathbf F
symbols.def: The Fréchet derivative of \(\mathbf F\) in the margin-source multinomial tangent space \(\{z\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal X_{T_0}\rvert}:\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}z=0\}\), evaluated at \(q_0\).

symbols.name: \widehat\Sigma
symbols.def: If every denominator appearing in \(\mathbf F(\widehat q_S,\widehat q_0)\) is strictly positive, define \[\widehat\phi_S(o)=\left.D_S\mathbf F\right|_{(\widehat q_S,\widehat q_0)}[e_o-\widehat q_S],\qquad \widehat\phi_0(o)=\left.D_0\mathbf F\right|_{(\widehat q_S,\widehat q_0)}[e_o-\widehat q_0],\] and \[\widehat\Sigma=\frac n{n_S}\sum_{o\in\mathcal X_V}\widehat q_S(o)\widehat\phi_S(o)\widehat\phi_S(o)^{\mathsf T}+\frac n{n_0}\sum_{o\in\mathcal X_{T_0}}\widehat q_0(o)\widehat\phi_0(o)\widehat\phi_0(o)^{\mathsf T}.\] If any such denominator is nonpositive, set \(\widehat\Sigma\) equal to the \(d\times d\) zero matrix.

assumptions.condition: Every substantive variable has a known finite state space and \(S\in\{0,1\}\).
\(M\) is recursive, semi-Markovian, and compatible with \(\mathcal G\).
The model-induced selected cells satisfy \(q_S^M(v)\ge\epsilon\) for every \(v\in\mathcal X_V\).

standard.name: Uniform cell positivity for a finite multinomial law

assumptions.condition: For the chosen representation \(\mathcal R\), every atom in the declared positive-support state space of every independent exogenous coordinate in \(\mathbf U\) has probability at least \(\eta\).

novel.justification: This is a representation-indexed interior restriction, not observed-law positivity. It holds for finite noisy response-type models whose positive-support mixing weights are uniformly separated from zero; after deleting zero-mass labels, every fixed finite representation satisfies it for some representation-specific \(\eta>0\).

assumptions.condition: \(O_1^S,\ldots,O_{n_S}^S\) are i.i.d. from \(q_S\), \(O_1^0,\ldots,O_{n_0}^0\) are i.i.d. from \(q_0\), and the two samples are independent.
Every denominator in the returned expression \(\mathbf F(q_S,q_0)\) is bounded below by a fixed positive constant.

standard.name: Interior differentiability of a finite probability functional

definitions.name: Positive selected-law SCM class
definitions.construction: \[\mathfrak M_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G)=\{M:\text{ \(M\) satisfies \(\mathrm{ass{:}finite\text{-}state}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}semi\text{-}markovian}\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}selection}\), and \(q_S^M(v)\ge\epsilon\) for every \(v\in\mathcal X_V\)}\}.\]

definitions.name: Compatible positive observed-data image
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)=\{\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M):M\in\mathfrak M_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G)\}.\] This is exactly the image of the positive graph-compatible model class; membership is not defined through existence of a separating pair.

definitions.name: Exact compatible observed-data fiber
definitions.construction: For \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\), \[\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)=\{M\in\mathfrak M_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G):\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M)=(q_S,q_0)\}.\]

definitions.name: Exact-fiber representation-indexed response-interior class
definitions.construction: \[\mathfrak R_{\epsilon,\eta}^{\circ}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)=\{(M,\mathcal R,U_0): M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0),\ \mathcal R\text{ is a finite independent response representation of }M,\ U_0\in\mathbf U,\text{ every coordinate state space in }\mathbf U\text{ equals its positive support, and every atom in every such state space has mass at least }\eta\}.\]

definitions.name: Finite arithmetic expression language
definitions.construction: For a fixed input \((q_S,q_0)\), \(\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\) is the smallest class of scalar expressions containing every cell of \(q_S\) and \(q_0\) and closed under finite addition, multiplication, and division by an expression whose value at that input is positive. A successful cell run returns one \(F_{x,y}\in\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\); causal validity is asserted only when \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\).

definitions.name: Exact probability-calculus transitions
definitions.construction: For every source tag \(s\), intervention block \(B\), conditioning block \(C\), disjoint nonempty blocks \(A,H\), and fixed output cell, the following are the complete scalar probability-calculus moves. Marginalization requires the \(\lvert\mathcal X_H\rvert\) input keys \(\{(A\cup H,B,C,s,(a,h),b,c):h\in\mathcal X_H\}\), outputs \((A,B,C,s,a,b,c)\), and stores \(E_{\mathrm{out}}=\sum_hE_\sigma(A\cup H,B,C,s,(a,h),b,c)\); it introduces no denominator. Conditioning requires all \(\lvert\mathcal X_A\rvert\) keys \(\{(A\cup H,B,C,s,(a',h),b,c):a'\in\mathcal X_A\}\), outputs \((A,B,C\cup H,s,a,b,(c,h))\), and stores the annotation at \((a,h)\) divided by the sum over \(a'\); it is admissible exactly when that denominator is positive. Chain composition has arity two: inputs \((A,B,C,s,a,b,c)\) and \((H,B,C\cup A,s,h,b,(c,a))\), output \((A\cup H,B,C,s,(a,h),b,c)\), and stored product of the two scalar annotations. The symmetric chain instance interchanges \(A,H\); only the lexicographically first representation of an identical output scalar key is eligible. Each required input and output belongs to \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\), and each move instance records its complete finite input-key set.

definitions.name: Exact population and selection-aware graphical fixing transitions
definitions.construction: Write \(G_{\overline B}\) for \(\mathcal G\) with arrows into \(B\) removed, \(G_{\overline B,\underline H}\) also with arrows out of \(H\) removed, and \(H_s(C)=H\setminus\operatorname{An}_{G_{\overline B}}(C\cup S_s)\). For \(s\in\{\mathrm{pop},\mathrm{sel}\}\), each scalar transition has arity one, retains its source tag, copies the input annotation, and introduces no denominator. Rule \(1\) maps \((A,B,C\cup H,s,a,b,(c,h))\leftrightarrow(A,B,C,s,a,b,c)\) when \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp H\mid B,C,S_s\) in \(G_{\overline B}\). Rule \(2\) maps \((A,B,C\cup H,s,a,b,(c,h))\leftrightarrow(A,B\cup H,C,s,a,(b,h),c)\) when \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp H\mid B,C,S_s\) in \(G_{\overline B,\underline H}\). Rule \(3\) maps \((A,B\cup H,C,s,a,(b,h),c)\leftrightarrow(A,B,C,s,a,b,c)\) when \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp H\mid B,C,S_s\) in \(G_{\overline B,\overline{H_s(C)}}\). Each displayed reverse and each cell \((a,b,c,h)\) is a separate canonical move instance. The \(\mathrm{popfix}_r\) tags have \(s=\mathrm{pop}\), and \(\mathrm{selfix}_r\) have \(s=\mathrm{sel}\), so the latter condition every separation test on \(S=1\). Disjointness of \(A,B,C,H\), nonemptiness of \(A,H\), membership of both scalar keys in \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\), and definition of the displayed input cell are mandatory.

definitions.name: Exact margin-extension and population-storage transitions
definitions.construction: Margin extension has arity two at each cell. For nonempty \(Z\subseteq V\setminus T_0\), fixed \(t\in\mathcal X_{T_0}\), and fixed \(z\in\mathcal X_Z\), its only input keys are \((Z,\varnothing,T_0,\mathrm{sel},z,\ast,t)\) and \((T_0,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},t,\ast,\ast)\). If \(Z\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid T_0\) in \(\mathcal G\) and the selected conditional cell is defined, the output is \((T_0\cup Z,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},(t,z),\ast,\ast)\), with annotation equal to the product of the two input annotations. Population storage has arity one at each \((a,b,c)\): input \((A,B,C,\mathrm{sel},a,b,c)\), output \((A,B,C,\mathrm{pop},a,b,c)\), and unchanged annotation when \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid B,C\) in \(G_{\overline B}\). Every conditioning cell used by an input must have positive probability. These are the only source-changing moves, and every output belongs to \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\).

definitions.name: Canonical finite mixed-source saturation machine
definitions.construction: On input \((\mathcal G,X,Y,x,y,T_0,q_S,q_0)\), \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}\) initializes, for every \(v\in\mathcal X_V\), the scalar key \((V,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{sel},v,\ast,\ast)\) with annotation \(q_S(v)\) and provenance \(\mathrm{init}_S\). When \(T_0\ne\varnothing\), it also initializes, for every \(t\in\mathcal X_{T_0}\), \((T_0,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},t,\ast,\ast)\) with \(q_0(t)\) and provenance \(\mathrm{init}_0\); when \(T_0=V\), these are exactly all cells of the full population law. When \(T_0=\varnothing\), \(q_0\) is the unique trivial law, its scalar unit creates no key, and no margin-extension instance is admissible because its required nonempty population-margin input key is absent. Population storage remains admissible whenever its unchanged predicate \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid B,C\) in \(G_{\overline B}\) holds, including the corresponding unconditional selection-independence predicate when \(B=C=\varnothing\). At each state the scalar target key \((Y,X,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},y,x,\ast)\) is checked first. Otherwise the procedure scans \(\mathscr U\) in the order \(\mathrm{popstore},\mathrm{margin},\mathrm{popfix}_1,\mathrm{popfix}_2,\mathrm{popfix}_3,\mathrm{selfix}_1,\mathrm{selfix}_2,\mathrm{selfix}_3,\mathrm{marginal},\mathrm{condition},\mathrm{chain}\), then lexicographically, and takes the first instance whose exact premises hold, whose complete finite input-key set is contained in \(K_\sigma\), and whose one output scalar key is absent. It adds that output key, stores the displayed scalar arithmetic annotation and backpointer, and preserves all old entries. A present output is a duplicate and is skipped without overwrite. The target annotation is returned as \(F_{x,y}\); if no enabled instance has an absent output, \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) is returned. Formula spelling and derivation length never affect key identity or priority.

definitions.name: Finite full conditional-kernel collection
definitions.construction: Run \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}(\mathcal G,X,Y,x,y,T_0,q_S,q_0)\) separately for every \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\), in the fixed lexicographic order. If every run returns \(F_{x,y}\), collect the results as \(\mathbf F=(F_{x,y}:(x,y)\in\mathcal I)^{\mathsf T}\), with coordinates indexed against the target table \(\boldsymbol\psi(M)\). If any run returns \(\operatorname{FAIL}\), report the set of failed cells and do not form \(\mathbf F\).

definitions.name: Representation-indexed projective source row space
definitions.construction: On the active index set \(\mathcal J_0\), with \(\mathbf 1\) denoting the all-ones vector in \(\mathbb R^{\mathcal J_0}\), \[\Gamma_{(M,\mathcal R,U_0)}=\operatorname{span}\left(\mathbf 1,\{b_t:t\in\mathcal X_{T_0}\},\{(u^{\mathsf T}a_+)a_v-(u^{\mathsf T}a_v)a_+:v\in\mathcal X_V\}\right)\subseteq\mathbb R^{\mathcal J_0}.\] Every inner product and row is restricted to \(j\in\mathcal J_0\); no zero-mass response label contributes a coordinate.

definitions.name: Chosen-coordinate response-law perturbation
definitions.construction: For \(u^{\pm}_j=u_j\pm\tau\beta_j\) on \(j\in\mathcal J_0\) satisfying \(u^+,u^-\in\Delta(\mathcal J_0)^{\circ}\), let \(\mathcal R_1\) and \(\mathcal R_2\) retain every deterministic response map in \(\mathcal R\) and every exogenous-coordinate law other than that of \(U_0\), while assigning \(U_0\) the mass vectors \(u^+\) and \(u^-\), respectively, on the same declared state space \(\mathcal J_0\); let \(M_1\) and \(M_2\) be the induced SCMs.

definitions.name: Parameterized three-node exact audit
definitions.construction: For each enumerated binary graph with \(\lvert V\rvert\le3\), each enumerated query specification \((T_0,X,Y,x,y)\), and each canonical branch of the exact cell-key transition system, \(\operatorname{QE}_3\) treats every cell of \(q_S,q_0\) and \(\epsilon\) as free real parameters. Its parameter domain imposes the two simplex equations and inequalities, \(\epsilon>0\), \(q_S(v)\ge\epsilon\) for every \(v\), and the compatible-image condition \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\) through existential graph-compatible response weights and a positive selection normalizer. The branch formula literally replays \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\), source tags, graphical predicates, every positive-denominator condition, duplicate rule, and canonical priority of \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}\). Each response coordinate is indexed exactly by its positive support; support sign conditions are retained inside the real-closed-field formula, every normalized latent vector ranges only over its positive-support atoms, and all rows \(u,a_v,a_+,b_t,h_{x,y}\) use only those active coordinates. On a success branch, the eliminated counterexample formula existentially quantifies a graph-compatible response law and positive selection normalizer satisfying the exact-fiber equations \(P_M(V=v,S=1)=q_S(v)P_M(S=1)\), \(P_M(T_0=t)=q_0(t)\), and \(F_{x,y}(q_S,q_0)\ne\psi_{x,y}(M)\); emptiness of that formula certifies equality for every represented model in the exact fiber. On a failure branch, two separately quantified graph-compatible response laws must share the same symbolic \(q_S,q_0\), satisfy positive selection normalizers and all of those exact fiber equalities, have atoms on their respective positive-support state spaces bounded below by one common existential \(\eta>0\), and have unequal scalar query cells. Clearing a denominator is permitted only after adding its strict positivity constraint. Real-closed-field elimination removes all response weights, normalizers, and \(\eta\), and cylindrical algebraic decomposition returns a finite semialgebraic partition of the symbolic \((q_S,q_0,\epsilon)\) domain with, on every cell, the successful-formula certificate or the exact same-input separating-witness certificate. No observed table or input fiber is enumerated.

definitions.name: Saturated two-source plug-in estimator
definitions.construction: When all cell runs return differentiable expressions, collect them using \(\mathrm{def{:}full\text{-}kernel\text{-}collection}\). If every denominator appearing in \(\mathbf F(\widehat q_S,\widehat q_0)\) is strictly positive, set \[\widehat{\mathbf F}=\bigl(F_{x,y}(\widehat q_S,\widehat q_0):(x,y)\in\mathcal I\bigr)^{\mathsf T}=\mathbf F(\widehat q_S,\widehat q_0).\] Otherwise set \(\widehat{\mathbf F}=0\in\mathbb R^d\).

definitions.name: Source-specific multinomial-tangent influence functions
definitions.construction: With \(D_S\mathbf F\) and \(D_0\mathbf F\) interpreted as linear maps on their zero-sum multinomial tangent spaces, \[\phi_S(o)=D_S\mathbf F[e_o-q_S],\qquad \phi_0(o)=D_0\mathbf F[e_o-q_0],\qquad \Sigma=\lambda^{-1}\operatorname{Var}_{q_S}(\phi_S)+(1-\lambda)^{-1}\operatorname{Var}_{q_0}(\phi_0).\] The centered one-hot residuals belong to the stated tangent spaces, so no dimension-mismatched free-coordinate multiplication occurs.

definitions.name: Fixed positive compact inference class
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal K=\{(q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0):\text{ \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}denominators}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}covariance\text{-}nondegenerate}\) hold, and \((q_S,q_0)\) lies in a fixed compact subset of the relative interior}\}.\] The selected-cell lower bound follows from membership in \(\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\).

definitions.name: Studentized simultaneous confidence region
definitions.construction: \[\widehat C_{1-\alpha}=\begin{cases}\left\{z\in\mathbb R^d:\max_{1\le k\le d}\dfrac{\sqrt n\lvert\widehat{\mathbf F}_k-z_k\rvert}{\sqrt{\widehat\Sigma_{kk}}}\le c_{1-\alpha}\right\},&\min_{1\le k\le d}\widehat\Sigma_{kk}>0,\\ \mathbb R^d,&\min_{1\le k\le d}\widehat\Sigma_{kk}\le0.\end{cases}\]

statements.statement: Fix \(\epsilon>0\), \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\), and \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\). For any \(Z\subseteq V\setminus T_0\) such that \(Z\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid T_0\) in \(\mathcal G\), \[P_M(T_0,Z)=P_M(Z\mid T_0,S=1)q_0(T_0).\]
statements.justification: This identity is the sound primitive that converts one unbiased margin into a larger population kernel.
statements.gap: It restates Correa, Tian, and Bareinboim's Lemma 1 as the base case needed by the new recursion.
statements.consumer: It produces the population kernel used by the ACTG audit whenever the measured margin blocks selection from an additional covariate block.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a cell \(t\in\mathcal X_{T_0}\) and a cell \(z\in\mathcal X_Z\).  Because \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\), Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}model\text{-}class}\), \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}data\text{-}map}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}exact\text{-}observed\text{-}fiber}\) give
\[
 P_M(S=1)>0,\qquad P_M(V=v\mid S=1)=q_S(v)\geq\epsilon
 \quad\text{for every }v\in\mathcal X_V,
\]
and \(P_M(T_0=t)=q_0(t)\).  Summing the selected cells over all full cells whose \(T_0\)-coordinate is \(t\) shows
\[
 P_M(T_0=t\mid S=1)
 =\sum_{v:v_{T_0}=t}q_S(v)>0.
\]
Consequently \(P_M(T_0=t,S=1)>0\), hence also \(P_M(T_0=t)>0\); every conditional probability used below is therefore defined.

By \(\mathrm{ass{:}semi\text{-}markovian}\), compatibility with \(\mathcal G\) gives the global Markov implication for the stated graphical separation.  Thus \(Z\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid T_0\) in \(\mathcal G\) implies
\[
 P_M(Z=z\mid T_0=t,S=1)=P_M(Z=z\mid T_0=t).
\]
Multiplication by the positive population margin and then use of the exact-fiber equality yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_M(T_0=t,Z=z)
 &=P_M(Z=z\mid T_0=t)P_M(T_0=t)\\
 &=P_M(Z=z\mid T_0=t,S=1)q_0(t).
 \end{aligned}
\]
This holds cell by cell.  When \(T_0=\varnothing\), the same calculation uses the unique empty-block cell and the unit margin; when \(Z=\varnothing\), it reduces to the margin identity.  These cover all boundary cases in the statement.

statements.statement: Fix \(\epsilon>0\) and \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\). At every reachable state \(\sigma\), \(K_\sigma\subseteq\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\), and every present scalar key \(\xi=(A,B,C,s,a,b,c)\) has exactly one scalar annotation and backpointer in \(E_\sigma\). For every \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\), that annotation equals the cell \(k_\kappa^M(a\mid b,c)=P_M(A=a\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,S_s)\) whenever the conditioning cell is positive. Every transition has exactly the finite input-key set, source tags, graphical predicate, denominator condition, scalar output key, and stored scalar functional specified by its move definition. No move overwrites a key or uses an annotation as a state identity, and only margin extension or population storage changes a selected source into a population source.
statements.justification: This invariant is the formal firewall preventing a conditional selected table from being silently reused as a population kernel.
statements.gap: IDSB establishes soundness of its recursion; the enlarged saturation requires a key-level invariant that audits every probability, graphical-fixing, and source-bridge transition without treating formulas as state identities.
statements.consumer: A checker can replay each ACTG audit formula from its backpointers and reject any derivation that crosses source tags without a licensed bridge.
statements.proof_tex:
We prove the assertion by induction on the number of transitions from the initialized state in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\).

At initialization, the selected key indexed by a full cell \(v\) has annotation
\[
 q_S(v)=P_M(V=v\mid S=1),
\]
where the equality follows from membership of \(M\) in the exact fiber.  If \(T_0\neq\varnothing\), the population key indexed by \(t\) has annotation
\[
 q_0(t)=P_M(T_0=t).
\]
These are precisely the kernels named by their selected and population source tags.  The initialized keys belong to \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\), and each is assigned once with its prescribed initialization backpointer.

Assume the invariant before one transition.  For a marginalization transition, the induction hypothesis and finite additivity give, cell by cell,
\[
 \sum_{h\in\mathcal X_H}
 P_M(A=a,H=h\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,S_s)
 =P_M(A=a\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,S_s).
\]
For a conditioning transition, its required strict denominator condition and the induction hypothesis give
\[
 \frac{P_M(A=a,H=h\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,S_s)}
 {\sum_{a'\in\mathcal X_A}P_M(A=a',H=h\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,S_s)}
 =P_M(A=a\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,H=h,S_s).
\]
For a chain transition, the conditional product rule gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &P_M(A=a\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,S_s)\\
 &\qquad{}\times
 P_M(H=h\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,A=a,S_s)\\
 &=P_M(A=a,H=h\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,S_s).
 \end{aligned}
\]
All denominators invoked here are positive by the eligibility condition in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}probability\text{-}moves}\).

For any population or selected graphical-fixing transition, the relevant equality is exactly one of the sound do-calculus equivalences in Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}do\text{-}calculus\text{-}rules}\).  Its source tag is retained, and its conditioning cell is required to be positive.  For margin extension, Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}margin\text{-}extension}\) gives at every eligible \((t,z)\)
\[
 P_M(T_0=t,Z=z)
 =P_M(Z=z\mid T_0=t,S=1)q_0(t),
\]
which is the stored product.  Finally, for population storage the graphical premise \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid B,C\) in \(G_{\overline B}\), the positive selected conditioning cell, and Rule 1 of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}do\text{-}calculus\text{-}rules}\) imply
\[
 P_M(A=a\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c,S=1)
 =P_M(A=a\mid\operatorname{do}(B=b),C=c).
\]
Thus every possible transition stores the model kernel named by its output key.

The transition definitions require their complete finite input-key sets to be present and their output to lie in \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\) further requires that output to be absent, adds it once with one annotation and one backpointer, and preserves every old entry.  Therefore uniqueness and the inclusion \(K_\sigma\subseteq\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\) are preserved.  The list of move tags shows directly that probability and graphical-fixing moves retain \(s\), while the two source-bridge moves are the only transitions with selected input and population output.  This completes the induction.

statements.statement: For every finite syntactically valid cell input \((\mathcal G,X,Y,x,y,T_0,q_S,q_0)\), \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}\) terminates with at most \(\lvert\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\rvert\le2\{(1+3r)^{\lvert V\rvert}-(1+2r)^{\lvert V\rvert}\}\) scalar keys ever present: every nonterminal transition adds one previously absent scalar key and strictly decreases \(\mu(\sigma)\). Every legal move instance belongs to the finite universe \(\mathscr U\), and its output remains in \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\). Fix \(\epsilon>0\) and require \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\). If the procedure returns \(F_{x,y}\in\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\), then \[F_{x,y}(q_S,q_0)=\psi_{x,y}(M)=P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))\] for every \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\). Running the procedure over every \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\) therefore yields \(\mathbf F(q_S,q_0)=\boldsymbol\psi(M)\) for every model in that exact fiber whenever all cell runs succeed.
statements.justification: The bounded canonical key inventory makes both validity of every successful expression and termination independently auditable.
statements.gap: Correa, Tian, and Bareinboim prove IDSB sound; this claim gives an exact finite transition system, source-tag invariant, and graph-indexed termination measure for saturation over the same two observed laws, without claiming failure completeness.
statements.consumer: Every successful ACTG audit formula comes with a finite derivation trace that can be checked against the selected table and audited margin.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(d_W=\lvert\mathcal X_W\rvert\leq r\) for each \(W\in V\).  To specify a scalar key, each vertex is either absent, assigned to \(A\) with one of \(d_W\) cell values, assigned to \(B\) with one of \(d_W\) values, or assigned to \(C\) with one of \(d_W\) values.  Requiring \(A\neq\varnothing\) subtracts the assignments having no \(A\)-vertex, and the two source tags contribute a factor of two.  Hence Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\) and the inventory definition give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \lvert\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\rvert
 &=2\left\{\prod_{W\in V}(1+3d_W)-\prod_{W\in V}(1+2d_W)\right\}\\
 &\leq2\left\{(1+3r)^{\lvert V\rvert}-(1+2r)^{\lvert V\rvert}\right\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The first equality is also obtained by partitioning according to the disjoint sets \(A,B,C\) and then counting their cells.

The ordered instance universe \(\mathscr U\) is finite because \(V\), \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\), and the move-tag set are finite.  Every enabled nonterminal transition is, by definition, an instance in \(\mathscr U\) whose output is a key in \(\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\), and the absent-output condition gives
\[
 K_{\sigma'}=K_\sigma\cup\{\xi_{\mathrm{out}}\},
 \qquad \xi_{\mathrm{out}}\notin K_\sigma.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \mu(\sigma')
 =\lvert\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\setminus K_{\sigma'}\rvert
 =\mu(\sigma)-1.
\]
The nonnegative integer \(\mu\) can decrease only finitely many times.  Each intervening scan is over the finite ordered set \(\mathscr U\), so a scan either adds such a key, returns a present target, or returns \(\operatorname{FAIL}\).  Thus the procedure terminates and never has more than \(\lvert\mathscr K_{\mathcal G}\rvert\) keys present.

Now fix a compatible input and a model \(M\) in its exact fiber.  By Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}extid\text{-}storage\text{-}invariant}\), every annotation at every reachable state equals the interventional-kernel cell named by its key.  Finite sums and products preserve membership in \(\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\), and a division is performed only when its denominator is positive; induction on the transition count therefore also shows that every annotation is in \(\mathcal A(q_S,q_0)\).  If the target key is present, its key is
\[
 (Y,X,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},y,x,\ast),
\]
so its annotation satisfies
\[
 F_{x,y}(q_S,q_0)
 =P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))
 =\psi_{x,y}(M).
\]
The input tables are common to every \(M\) in the exact fiber, so the same equality holds simultaneously for every such model.  Applying the cell argument in the finite lexicographic order on \(\mathcal I\) and using Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}full\text{-}kernel\text{-}collection}\) gives, whenever all runs succeed,
\[
 \mathbf F(q_S,q_0)=\{\psi_{x,y}(M):(x,y)\in\mathcal I\}
 =\boldsymbol\psi(M)
\]
for every model in the fiber.

statements.justification: The representation index and explicit step-size bound turn the null-space argument into a valid interior SCM construction rather than a model-level shorthand.
statements.gap: Kivva et al. perturb response laws under unnormalized source constraints; the normalized selected-law cross-product rows and independent margin rows are specific to this two-law fiber.
statements.consumer: A terminal graph construction only needs to establish query-row separation; this theorem then produces the exact paired witness with controlled atom masses.
statements.proof_tex:
For brevity set
\[
 A_0=u^{\mathsf T}a_+,
 \qquad N_v=u^{\mathsf T}a_v,
 \qquad \delta_+=\beta^{\mathsf T}a_+,
 \qquad \delta_v=\beta^{\mathsf T}a_v.
\]
The law of total probability over the positive-support atoms \(j\in\mathcal J_0\), using independence of \(U_0\) from the other exogenous coordinates in \(\mathcal R\), gives
\[
 P_M(V=v,S=1)=\sum_j u_j a_v(j)=N_v,
 \qquad P_M(S=1)=\sum_j u_j a_+(j)=A_0>0.
\]
Thus \(q_S(v)=N_v/A_0\).  The identical calculation for the margin and intervened response gives
\[
 q_0(t)=P_M(T_0=t)=u^{\mathsf T}b_t,
 \qquad
 \psi_{x,y}(M)=u^{\mathsf T}h_{x,y}.
\]

Because \(\Gamma_{(M,\mathcal R,U_0)}\) is a finite-dimensional subspace and \(h_{x,y}\notin\Gamma_{(M,\mathcal R,U_0)}\), subtracting the orthogonal projection of \(h_{x,y}\) onto \(\Gamma_{(M,\mathcal R,U_0)}\) produces a nonzero \(\beta\in\Gamma_{(M,\mathcal R,U_0)}^\perp\) with
\[
 \beta^{\mathsf T}h_{x,y}=\lVert\beta\rVert_2^2>0.
\]
Orthogonality to \(\mathbf 1\), to each \(b_t\), and to each selected cross-product row gives
\[
 \beta^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1=0,
 \qquad \beta^{\mathsf T}b_t=0,
 \qquad A_0\delta_v-N_v\delta_+=0
 \quad\text{for every }t,v.
\]

The prescribed step-size bound is well defined because \(\beta\neq0\).  For every active atom,
\[
 u_j^\pm
 \geq u_j-\lvert\tau\rvert\lVert\beta\rVert_\infty
 \geq\eta/2>0,
 \qquad
 \sum_j u_j^\pm=1\pm\tau\beta^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1=1.
\]
Hence both vectors are probability vectors on exactly the unchanged positive support \(\mathcal J_0\).  Every other exogenous atom retains mass at least \(\eta\), so every atom in each perturbed representation has mass at least \(\eta/2\).

Since \(A_0>0\), at least one \(a_+(j)>0\).  All \(u_j^\pm\) are positive and all \(a_+(j)\) are nonnegative, so
\[
 (u^\pm)^{\mathsf T}a_+=A_0\pm\tau\delta_+>0.
\]
For each \(v\), the cross-product equality above yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac{(u^\pm)^{\mathsf T}a_v}{(u^\pm)^{\mathsf T}a_+}
 &=\frac{N_v\pm\tau\delta_v}{A_0\pm\tau\delta_+}\\
 &=\frac{N_v}{A_0}=q_S(v),
 \end{aligned}
\]
where the middle equality follows after cross multiplication from \(A_0\delta_v=N_v\delta_+\).  Similarly,
\[
 (u^\pm)^{\mathsf T}b_t=u^{\mathsf T}b_t=q_0(t).
\]
Thus both perturbed models reproduce the two observed tables exactly, and in particular preserve every selected lower bound \(q_S(v)\geq\epsilon\).

Only the atom masses of one independent exogenous coordinate are changed; the deterministic response maps, their parent arguments, and every other independent exogenous law are unchanged.  Therefore both induced SCMs remain recursive, semi-Markovian, and compatible with \(\mathcal G\).  The preceding positivity facts place their represented triples in \(\mathfrak R_{\epsilon,\eta/2}^{\circ}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\).  Finally,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \psi_{x,y}(M_1)-\psi_{x,y}(M_2)
 &=(u+\tau\beta)^{\mathsf T}h_{x,y}
 -(u-\tau\beta)^{\mathsf T}h_{x,y}\\
 &=2\tau\beta^{\mathsf T}h_{x,y}\neq0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Each query is a convex combination of entries of \(h_{x,y}\in[0,1]^{\mathcal J_0}\), so it remains in \([0,1]\).  This proves every assertion.

statements.statement: Fix \(\mathcal G,X,Y,x,y,T_0\) and \(\epsilon>0\). For every compatible input \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\) on which \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}(\mathcal G,X,Y,x,y,T_0,q_S,q_0)\) reaches a terminal \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) state, does there exist a common response-representation slack \(\eta>0\), quantified after that failed input, and a graph-compatible represented baseline \((M,\mathcal R,U_0)\in\mathfrak R_{\epsilon,\eta}^{\circ}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\) whose chosen-coordinate state space is exactly its positive support \(\mathcal J_0\) and whose active-coordinate query row satisfies \(h_{x,y}\notin\Gamma_{(M,\mathcal R,U_0)}\subseteq\mathbb R^{\mathcal J_0}\)? Thus the baseline must belong to the exact fiber \(\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\), and the projective certificate must produce two graph-compatible models in that same exact fiber that reproduce both input tables exactly and separate \(\psi_{x,y}\). The Handle is to extract the terminal do-calculus separation obstructions recorded by the scalar-key backpointers, splice classical hedge response maps across the obstructed districts, select one exogenous coordinate \(U_0\) with state space \(\mathcal J_0\) equal to its positive support, and solve the normalized selected-law cross-product and external-margin row constraints on those active coordinates inside the exact fiber, allowing the positive atom slack to depend on the compatible failed input.
statements.justification: After the named three-node gate succeeds, this representation-indexed margin-anchored hedge is the genuinely open universal necessity step behind a complete decision rule.
statements.gap: Ordinary hedges preserve one full observational law, and positive gID witnesses preserve unnormalized interventional sources; neither result preserves a normalized selected conditional and a separately fixed population margin on the same SCM fiber.
statements.consumer: A positive answer turns every rejected WIHS or CNICS margin into an explicit nonrecoverability certificate; a negative answer identifies a missing legal move for the state machine.

statements.statement: After the \(\mathcal G_\star\) interior gate is certified, for every binary selection ADMG with \(\lvert V\rvert\le3\), every \(T_0\subseteq V\), every disjoint query \((X,Y)\), every cell \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\), every \(\epsilon>0\), and every compatible input \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\), does parameterized exact response-function elimination certify every scalar formula returned by \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}(\mathcal G,X,Y,x,y,T_0,q_S,q_0)\), find no identified cell on which it returns \(\operatorname{FAIL}\), and, for every nonidentified failure, produce two graph-compatible models in the exact fiber \(\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\) with atoms on their exact positive-support state spaces bounded below by one common \(\eta>0\) that may depend on the failed input and with unequal query-cell values? The Handle enumerates only the finite graphs, query specifications \((T_0,X,Y,x,y)\), and canonical \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}\) branches, beginning with \(\mathcal G_\star\). For each branch it leaves \(q_S,q_0,\epsilon\) symbolic under simplex, positivity, and compatible-image constraints, literally replays every scalar-key predicate and denominator check, eliminates response weights and positive selection normalizers in the real closed field, and returns a finite cylindrical-algebraic semialgebraic partition carrying either universal successful-formula equality or an exact same-input separating witness. No input table or observed-data fiber is enumerated.
statements.justification: The census is a required kill test before the universal margin-anchored hedge can be treated as a credible completeness route.
statements.gap: Duarte et al. provide the polynomial response-function encoding but do not classify this exact selected-conditional-plus-independent-margin decision problem over all three-node graphs.
statements.consumer: Any collision isolates the smallest unsound rule or incomplete terminal state before the universal proof is attempted.

statements.statement: Conditional first on an affirmative fully interior certificate for the \(\mathcal G_\star\) terminal cell failure, then on successful completion of the remaining exact three-node cell audit with no collision, and finally on an affirmative resolution of the margin-anchored hedge question for every terminal cell failure, fix \(\mathcal G,X,Y,x,y,T_0\), \(\epsilon>0\), and \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\). Every \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) output then admits a slack \(\eta>0\), chosen after this failed compatible input, and two finite graph-compatible models \(M_1,M_2\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\), with \((M_1,\mathcal R_1,U_0),(M_2,\mathcal R_2,U_0)\in\mathfrak R_{\epsilon,\eta/2}^{\circ}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\), such that \(\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_1)=\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M_2)=(q_S,q_0)\) exactly and \(\psi_{x,y}(M_1)\ne\psi_{x,y}(M_2)\). Under these three discharged premises, the cell-indexed \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}\) is sound and complete on \(\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\) cell by cell, and the finite collection over \(\mathcal I\) decides recovery of the full table \(\boldsymbol\psi(M)\) on each exact observed-data fiber.
statements.justification: This is an integration corollary recording what follows after the three-node gates and the focal margin-anchored hedge theorem are discharged.
statements.gap: Correa, Tian, and Bareinboim leave completeness of IDSB for these exact two laws unresolved; the substantive new step is the universal projective failure certificate, not this conditional composition.
statements.consumer: Once all three premises are proved, an ACTG 320 generalization audit can certify whether a proposed WIHS or CNICS margin is sufficient or provably insufficient.

statements.statement: Qiu et al.'s external-data result and the present decision problem overlap only on a restricted boundary. Their Appendix B.2, Condition 2 and Theorem B.5 take \(P(V\mid S=1)\) together with the unbiased covariate margin \(P(T_0)\) and characterize identification of the scalar \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}\) under unconfoundedness, treatment overlap, and specified probability classes for the propensity, covariate-outcome law, and selection law. That boundary is contained in the present input signature when \(T_0\) is the covariate block. Their theorem does not decide each scalar cell \(\psi_{x,y}\), or their finite full-table collection \(\boldsymbol\psi\), for an arbitrary finite-state semi-Markovian ADMG, while the present graph-only model does not imply their probability-class restrictions and does not contain their continuous-law examples. Thus the results have a nonempty special-case intersection but neither theorem subsumes the other.
statements.justification: This primary-text comparison prevents a scalar probability-class ATE frontier from being mistaken for completeness over the arbitrary two-law ADMG fiber.
statements.gap: Qiu et al. give a necessary-and-sufficient probability-class condition for full-population ATE, whereas the focal open question is a graph-compatible same-input witness for every failed arbitrary interventional-distribution query.
statements.consumer: The ACTG audit can use Qiu et al.'s theorem when its unconfounded scalar-ATE boundary applies and reserve EXT-ID for graph-indexed queries outside that boundary.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(C\), \(D\), and \(R\) denote, respectively, the covariate block, binary treatment, and outcome in the cited Qiu et al. result \texttt{lem:qiu-external-ate-characterization}. Reindex those variables in the present notation by
\[
T_0=C,\qquad X=\{D\},\qquad Y=\{R\},\qquad V=C\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{D,R\}.
\]
The unions are disjoint by the roles of covariate, treatment, and outcome in that result. By \texttt{def:observed-data-map}, the present two-source observation on this boundary is
\[
\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M)
=\bigl(P_M(V\mid S=1),P_M(T_0)\bigr)
=\bigl(P_M(C,D,R\mid S=1),P_M(C)\bigr)
=\bigl(q_S^M,q_0^M\bigr).
\]
These are exactly the two kinds of input in \texttt{lem:qiu-external-ate-characterization}. Thus, when \(T_0\) is the covariate block, Qiu et al.'s external-data problem is a specialization of the present input signature.

The named unconfoundedness and overlap restrictions in that result, written after the same reindexing, are
\[
\bigl(R(0),R(1)\bigr)\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}D\mid C,
\qquad
0<P_M(D=1\mid C=c)<1
\quad\text{for every }c\in\operatorname{supp}(P_M(C)).
\]
The support qualification makes the displayed conditional probabilities well defined. These are source-side restrictions, not consequences of the input equality above.

There is also a genuine overlap in the causal targets. On the finite subcase in which \(R\) is numeric and \(D\) is binary, the definitions of \(\psi_{x,y}\) and \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}\), followed by the finite expectation identity, give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}(M)
&=E_M[R\mid\operatorname{do}(D=1)]-E_M[R\mid\operatorname{do}(D=0)]\\
&=\sum_{r\in\mathcal X_R}r\,P_M(R=r\mid\operatorname{do}(D=1))
  -\sum_{r\in\mathcal X_R}r\,P_M(R=r\mid\operatorname{do}(D=0))\\
&=\sum_{r\in\mathcal X_R}r\,\psi_{1,r}(M)
  -\sum_{r\in\mathcal X_R}r\,\psi_{0,r}(M).
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence the scalar target of the cited theorem is a computable linear contrast of the present finite full table \(\boldsymbol\psi(M)\). This proves the claimed nonempty special-case intersection at the level of input and target signatures.

The first non-subsumption direction follows both from the cited theorem's hypotheses and from its scalar conclusion. By \texttt{lem:qiu-external-ate-characterization}, its conclusion assumes unconfoundedness and treatment overlap and identifies only \(\theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}\). In contrast, \texttt{def:model-class} permits an arbitrary finite-state recursive semi-Markovian model compatible with \(\mathcal G\), including ADMGs with latent treatment--outcome confounding, and \texttt{def:full-kernel-collection} asks separately for every coordinate \(\psi_{x,y}\). Moreover, the linear contrast above is not injective, even on strictly interior binary kernels. To see this within finite recursive SCMs, let \(C\) be constant, let \(U_D,U_S\) be independent fair binary variables, and let \(U_R\) be independent and uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,12\}\). In both models set \(D=U_D\) and \(S=U_S\). Define
\[
R_1=\mathbf 1\{U_R\le 3+6D\},
\qquad
R_2=\mathbf 1\{U_R\le 4+6D\}.
\]
Each construction is a finite recursive Markovian, hence semi-Markovian, SCM on the DAG \(D\to R\) with \(C\) and \(S\) isolated. All four selected \((D,R_j)\)-cells are positive; their minima are \(1/8\) and \(1/12\), respectively. Direct evaluation gives
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc|c}
 & P(R_j=1\mid\operatorname{do}(D=0))
 & P(R_j=1\mid\operatorname{do}(D=1))
 & \theta_{\mathrm{ATE}}\\ \hline
j=1 & 3/12 & 9/12 & 6/12\\
j=2 & 4/12 & 10/12 & 6/12.
\end{array}
\]
Thus both ATEs equal \(1/2\), while, for example, the \((D=0,R=1)\) interventional cells are \(1/4\) and \(1/3\). Consequently, identification of the scalar ATE cannot by itself decide the coordinates of \(\boldsymbol\psi\); a fortiori the cited scalar theorem is not a completeness theorem for the present arbitrary-cell ADMG decision problem.

For the reverse direction, \texttt{def:model-class} and its finite-state support requirement imply that every substantive law in the present model class has finite support. The cited Qiu et al. setup, by contrast, includes covariate--outcome laws having densities on Euclidean spaces and continuous probability-family examples. Such laws are outside the present finite-state class. In addition, Qiu et al.'s Condition 2 is a condition on an explicitly chosen triple of probability classes and quantifies over pairs of compatible laws in those classes. Compatibility with a graph \(\mathcal G\) alone supplies no such choice: changing the positive exogenous mass functions or structural kernels while leaving \(\mathcal G\) fixed changes the propensity, outcome, and selection laws without changing the graph. Therefore the present graph-only premises do not imply Qiu et al.'s probability-class condition, and the present finite-state result cannot subsume their continuous-law cases.

The two directions together prove that the common selected-law-plus-margin, scalar-ATE boundary is nonempty, while neither result subsumes the other.

statements.statement: Fix \(\epsilon>0\), \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\), \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\), and a cell \((x,y)\). The exact transition system has four audited reductions. If \(T_0=V\), initialization stores every scalar cell \(q_0(v)=P_M(V=v)\) at \((V,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},v,\ast,\ast)\); consequently, whenever \(\psi_{x,y}\) is identifiable from the full population law by a finite sequence of ordinary do-calculus and probability moves, the saturation returns a valid arithmetic functional for that cell. If \(\mathcal G\) entails \(S\perp\!\!\!\perp V\), population storage inserts the same full-population scalar keys with annotations \(q_S(v)=P_M(V=v)\). If \(T_0=\varnothing\), the external-margin law is trivial, its scalar unit creates no key, and no margin-extension instance is admissible. The resulting boundary is the selected-source scalar closure augmented by exactly the population kernels inserted from a selected key \((A,B,C,\mathrm{sel},a,b,c)\) when \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid B,C\) in \(G_{\overline B}\), together with their consequences under the unchanged population graphical-fixing and probability moves; at \(B=C=\varnothing\), the storage predicate is unconditional selection independence. Whenever margin extension reconstructs every cell of \(P_M(V)\), the same qualified full-law conclusion holds; in particular, under the corresponding adjustment or front-door graphical criterion, the saturation returns a valid expression equal to the standard adjustment or front-door functional. Collecting all successful \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\) gives the corresponding identified coordinates of the full conditional-kernel table on the exact fiber.
statements.justification: Direct initialization and source tags make the full-law, ignorable-selection, corrected empty-margin-with-licensed-storage, and reconstructed-law boundaries actual branches of the algorithm.
statements.gap: These are regression reductions to established ID and IDSB results rather than novelty claims.
statements.consumer: They provide executable boundary tests before the ACTG graph and margin are audited.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume the proposed, qualified statement.  If \(T_0=V\), the population initialization clause in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\), together with exact-fiber membership, gives for every \(v\)
\[
 E_\sigma(V,\varnothing,\varnothing,\mathrm{pop},v,\ast,\ast)
 =q_0(v)=P_M(V=v).
\]
Every finite derivation using ordinary probability manipulations and the three do-calculus rules can be replayed by the corresponding population-tagged instances of Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}probability\text{-}moves}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}graphical\text{-}fixing\text{-}moves}\).  Canonical priority cannot prevent this replay: induct on the length of the finite derivation.  Once all inputs of its next move are present, either its output is already present or that instance remains enabled until it is added; only finitely many absent keys can be added before it.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}ordinary\text{-}do\text{-}calculus\text{-}completeness}\) supplies such a finite derivation whenever the cell is ordinarily identifiable from \(P_M(V)\).  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}extid\text{-}storage\text{-}invariant}\) then proves validity of whichever target annotation canonical priority returns.

If \(S\perp\!\!\!\perp V\) is entailed by \(\mathcal G\), the population-storage instance with \(A=V\) and \(B=C=\varnothing\) is admissible.  Independence and exact-fiber membership give
\[
 q_S(v)=P_M(V=v\mid S=1)=P_M(V=v),
\]
so that transition inserts the claimed population key and annotation.

If \(T_0=\varnothing\), Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}extid\text{-}state\text{-}machine}\) creates no population key from the unit margin.  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}source\text{-}bridge\text{-}moves}\) requires a nonempty population-margin input for margin extension, so no such instance is admissible.  Inspection of the complete move-tag list then shows that population storage is the only remaining selected-to-population transition.  Its exact graphical predicate is
\[
 A\perp\!\!\!\perp S\mid B,C
 \quad\text{in }G_{\overline B},
\]
which becomes unconditional selection independence when \(B=C=\varnothing\).  All subsequent population keys arise only through the source-preserving population probability and graphical-fixing moves.  This proves the asserted exact empty-margin closure.

Finally, if repeated margin extension reconstructs every full-population cell, those annotations equal \(P_M(V=v)\) by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}margin\text{-}extension}\) and the storage invariant.  The same finite-derivation replay used in the \(T_0=V\) case therefore applies.  Adjustment and front-door derivations are particular finite do-calculus derivations under their respective graphical criteria, so their returned annotations equal their standard functionals.  Applying this argument independently to every successful cell gives the final coordinatewise collection claim.  The qualification is necessary: without an identification criterion, a full observational law in a hidden-variable ADMG does not in general identify every intervention cell.

statements.statement: Fix \(\epsilon>0\), \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\), and \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\). If every cell run over \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\) returns a differentiable \(F_{x,y}\), then \(\mathbf F(q_S,q_0)=\boldsymbol\psi(M)\), and the saturated two-source plug-in estimator obeys \[\sqrt n\{\widehat{\mathbf F}-\mathbf F\}=\frac{\sqrt n}{n_S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_S}\phi_S(O_i^S)+\frac{\sqrt n}{n_0}\sum_{j=1}^{n_0}\phi_0(O_j^0)+o_P(1)\rightsquigarrow N(0,\Sigma).\]
statements.justification: This is a supporting finite-dimensional delta-method result that preserves source-specific uncertainty for compiled formulas.
statements.gap: The contribution is implementation support, not a new efficiency theorem; it instantiates the standard multinomial delta method for two independent tables.
statements.consumer: The expansion attributes uncertainty to selected records and audited margin records in the ACTG analysis.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(p=(q_S,q_0)\) and \(\widehat p=(\widehat q_S,\widehat q_0)\).  First, the soundness conclusion for the successful EXT-ID runs gives, cell by cell,
\[
F_{x,y}(q_S,q_0)=\psi_{x,y}(M)
\qquad ((x,y)\in\mathcal I)
\]
for every \(M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\).  The definition of the lexicographically ordered full-kernel collection therefore gives
\[
\mathbf F(q_S,q_0)=\boldsymbol\psi(M).
\]
This step uses the EXT-ID soundness theorem; it does not define the causal target to equal the observed-law functional.

We next derive the stochastic expansion.  The empirical residuals are in the declared multinomial tangent spaces because
\[
\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}(e_o-q_S)=0,
\qquad
\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}(e_o-q_0)=0.
\]
Consequently the source derivatives in the influence-function definition may be applied to them.  Linearity gives the exact identities
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_S\mathbf F[\widehat q_S-q_S]
&=\frac1{n_S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_S}
D_S\mathbf F[e_{O_i^S}-q_S]
=\frac1{n_S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_S}\phi_S(O_i^S),\\
D_0\mathbf F[\widehat q_0-q_0]
&=\frac1{n_0}\sum_{j=1}^{n_0}
D_0\mathbf F[e_{O_j^0}-q_0]
=\frac1{n_0}\sum_{j=1}^{n_0}\phi_0(O_j^0).
\end{aligned}
\]
For a probability vector \(q\) on a finite set and its empirical table \(\widehat q_N\), direct calculation yields
\[
\mathbb E_q\|\widehat q_N-q\|_2^2
=\frac1N\sum_o q(o)\{1-q(o)\}
=\frac{1-\sum_o q(o)^2}{N}\le \frac1N.
\]
The inequality
\[
\mathbf 1\{\|R\|_2>u\}\le \|R\|_2^2/u^2
\]
then shows that \(\widehat q_S-q_S=O_P(n_S^{-1/2})\) and \(\widehat q_0-q_0=O_P(n_0^{-1/2})\).  The sample-share assumption implies that \(n_S\), \(n_0\), and \(n\) have the same order.

By differentiability of the returned finite-dimensional map at \(p\),
\[
\mathbf F(\widehat p)-\mathbf F(p)
=D_S\mathbf F[\widehat q_S-q_S]
+D_0\mathbf F[\widehat q_0-q_0]+r_n,
\qquad
\frac{\|r_n\|_2}{\|\widehat q_S-q_S\|_2+\|\widehat q_0-q_0\|_2}
\xrightarrow{P}0.
\]
Every population denominator is strictly positive by the positive-denominator assumption.  Because there are finitely many continuous denominators, there is a neighborhood of \(p\) on which they remain positive.  The empirical tables enter this neighborhood with probability tending to one by the preceding bound.  Thus the zero fallback in the totalized plug-in definition is used with probability tending to zero and does not alter the displayed first-order expansion.  Hence \(r_n=o_P(n^{-1/2})\), and multiplication by \(\sqrt n\) gives the asserted asymptotic linear representation.

It remains to identify its limit.  The influence vectors are centered:
\[
\mathbb E_{q_S}\phi_S(O^S)
=D_S\mathbf F\!\left[\sum_o q_S(o)(e_o-q_S)\right]=0,
\qquad
\mathbb E_{q_0}\phi_0(O^0)=0.
\]
Form one triangular row from the mutually independent vectors
\[
R_{n,i}=\frac{\sqrt n}{n_S}\phi_S(O_i^S),
\quad 1\le i\le n_S,
\qquad
R_{n,n_S+j}=\frac{\sqrt n}{n_0}\phi_0(O_j^0),
\quad 1\le j\le n_0.
\]
The state spaces are finite, so both influence vectors are bounded.  Since \(\sqrt n/n_S=O(n^{-1/2})\) and \(\sqrt n/n_0=O(n^{-1/2})\), for every \(u>0\) all summands have norm at most \(u\) for sufficiently large \(n\); the Lindeberg sum is therefore eventually zero.  Independence of the two samples and the sample-share limit give
\[
\sum_{\ell=1}^{n}\operatorname{Cov}(R_{n,\ell})
=\frac n{n_S}\operatorname{Var}_{q_S}(\phi_S)
+\frac n{n_0}\operatorname{Var}_{q_0}(\phi_0)
\longrightarrow
\lambda^{-1}\operatorname{Var}_{q_S}(\phi_S)
+(1-\lambda)^{-1}\operatorname{Var}_{q_0}(\phi_0)
=\Sigma.
\]
The cited multivariate Lindeberg--Feller theorem now yields convergence of the linear term to \(N(0,\Sigma)\).  The cited asymptotic-equivalence theorem absorbs the \(o_P(1)\) remainder.  This proves both the displayed expansion and the claimed limit law.

statements.statement: For the fixed all-cell dimension \(d=\lvert\mathcal I\rvert\) and fixed positive compact class \(\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\), suppose that at every \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal K\), every cell run over \((x,y)\in\mathcal I\) succeeds and returns the same differentiable expressions \(F_{x,y}\); fix the resulting \(\mathbf F\). Then the plug-in covariance estimator satisfies, for every \(\delta>0\), \[\sup_{(q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal K}P_{q_S,q_0}\{\|\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}>\delta\}\longrightarrow0,\] and \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal K}\inf_{M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)}P_{q_S,q_0}\{\boldsymbol\psi(M)\in\widehat C_{1-\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha.\]
statements.justification: This supporting Bonferroni result supplies familywise coverage for a fixed vector of returned cells.
statements.gap: Uniform finite-table coverage on a positive compact set is standard and is not part of the completeness novelty claim.
statements.consumer: The ACTG audit can report one familywise-valid region for all prespecified treatment and outcome cells.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix the returned vector expression \(\mathbf F\) from the success branch in the proposed statement, write \(p=(q_S,q_0)\), and write \(P_p\) for the two-source sampling law at \(p\).  The finite arithmetic-language definition expresses every coordinate of \(\mathbf F\) as a rational function of finitely many probability cells.  On \(\mathcal K\), every denominator is bounded below by a common number \(\gamma>0\).  Since \(\mathcal K\) is compact and there are finitely many denominators, continuity supplies \(\rho>0\) such that every denominator is at least \(\gamma/2\) whenever a table pair lies within Euclidean distance \(\rho\) of \(\mathcal K\).  On this neighborhood \(\mathbf F\) is twice continuously differentiable, and compactness bounds its first and second derivatives by finite constants.  By continuity of the covariance formula and the assumed uniform positive lower bound on every coordinate variance, \(\rho\) may be decreased so that, once \(n_S/n\) is sufficiently close to \(\lambda\), every plug-in diagonal variance is positive throughout the same neighborhood.

Let \(\mathcal E_n(p)\) be the event
\[
\|\widehat q_S-q_S\|_2+\|\widehat q_0-q_0\|_2<\rho.
\]
The exact multinomial second-moment calculation from the source-specific proposition and the elementary inequality \(\mathbf 1\{R>u\}\le R^2/u^2\) imply
\[
\sup_{p\in\mathcal K}P_p\{\mathcal E_n(p)^c\}
\le \frac{4}{\rho^2n_S}+\frac{4}{\rho^2n_0}
\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus the fallback branches in the corrected plug-in, covariance, and confidence-region definitions have probability tending to zero uniformly over \(\mathcal K\).  On \(\mathcal E_n(p)\), the integral Taylor remainder and the uniform second-derivative bound give a constant \(C<\infty\), independent of \(p\in\mathcal K\), such that
\[
\left\|\mathbf F(\widehat p)-\mathbf F(p)
-D_S\mathbf F_p[\widehat q_S-q_S]
-D_0\mathbf F_p[\widehat q_0-q_0]\right\|_2
\le C\bigl(\|\widehat q_S-q_S\|_2+\|\widehat q_0-q_0\|_2\bigr)^2.
\]
Because the expectation of the squared quantity in parentheses is \(O(n^{-1})\) uniformly and \(n_S/n\to\lambda\in(0,1)\), another application of the same elementary probability bound shows that the Taylor remainder is \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) uniformly on \(\mathcal K\).

We next verify covariance consistency rather than assuming it.  For \(p\in\mathcal K\), set
\[
\begin{aligned}
\phi_{S,p}(o)&=D_S\mathbf F_p[e_o-q_S],
&V_S(p)&=\sum_{o\in\mathcal X_V}q_S(o)\phi_{S,p}(o)\phi_{S,p}(o)^{\mathsf T},\\
\phi_{0,p}(o)&=D_0\mathbf F_p[e_o-q_0],
&V_0(p)&=\sum_{o\in\mathcal X_{T_0}}q_0(o)\phi_{0,p}(o)\phi_{0,p}(o)^{\mathsf T}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The centering calculation in the preceding proposition shows that these second moments are the corresponding variances.  Hence
\[
\Sigma(p)=\lambda^{-1}V_S(p)+(1-\lambda)^{-1}V_0(p).
\]
By the corrected definition of the empirical covariance, on \(\mathcal E_n(p)\) it is the same finite formula with \(p\) replaced by \(\widehat p\) and \(\lambda\) replaced by \(n_S/n\).  That formula is continuous on the common neighborhood and uniformly continuous on its compact closure.  The uniform concentration bound and \(n_S/n\to\lambda\) therefore imply, for every \(\delta>0\),
\[
\sup_{p\in\mathcal K}P_p\{\|\widehat\Sigma-\Sigma(p)\|_{\mathrm{op}}>\delta\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The zero-matrix fallback contributes only on \(\mathcal E_n(p)^c\), whose probability has already been bounded uniformly.  This proves the first conclusion of the proposed statement.

For coverage, it remains to establish a uniform, rather than merely pointwise, central limit argument.  Suppose to the contrary that the asserted lower bound fails.  Then there are a number \(\eta>0\), a subsequence of sample sizes (not relabeled), points \(p_n=(q_{S,n},q_{0,n})\in\mathcal K\), and models \(M_n\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_{S,n},q_{0,n})\) such that the coverage probability is below \(1-\alpha-\eta\).  Compactness permits passage to a further subsequence for which \(p_n\to p_\star\in\mathcal K\).

For this triangular sequence define the independent centered summands
\[
R_{n,i}=\frac{\sqrt n}{n_S}\phi_{S,p_n}(O_i^S),
\qquad
R_{n,n_S+j}=\frac{\sqrt n}{n_0}\phi_{0,p_n}(O_j^0).
\]
Uniform boundedness of the first derivatives on the common neighborhood and finiteness of both state spaces imply
\[
\max_{1\le \ell\le n}\|R_{n,\ell}\|_2=O(n^{-1/2}),
\]
so the Lindeberg condition holds.  Continuity of \(V_S\) and \(V_0\), together with the sample-share limit, gives
\[
\sum_{\ell=1}^{n}\operatorname{Cov}_{p_n}(R_{n,\ell})
=\frac n{n_S}V_S(p_n)+\frac n{n_0}V_0(p_n)
\longrightarrow\Sigma(p_\star).
\]
The cited Lindeberg--Feller theorem, the uniform Taylor expansion, and the cited asymptotic-equivalence result yield
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat{\mathbf F}-\mathbf F(p_n)\}
\rightsquigarrow N\{0,\Sigma(p_\star)\}.
\]
Uniform covariance consistency also gives \(\widehat\Sigma\xrightarrow{P}\Sigma(p_\star)\) along this sequence.  The coordinatewise variance assumption supplies a common \(\underline\sigma>0\) with \(\Sigma_{kk}(p)\ge\underline\sigma\) for every \(p\in\mathcal K\) and every \(k\).  Define the studentized vector coordinatewise by
\[
T_{n,k}=\frac{\sqrt n\{\widehat{\mathbf F}_k-\mathbf F_k(p_n)\}}{\sqrt{\widehat\Sigma_{kk}}}
\]
when all diagonal entries of \(\widehat\Sigma\) are positive, and set \(T_n=0\) otherwise.  On the latter event the corrected confidence region is \(\mathbb R^d\), and \(0\) belongs to the Bonferroni rectangle, so
\[
\{\mathbf F(p_n)\in\widehat C_{1-\alpha}\}
=\left\{\max_{1\le k\le d}|T_{n,k}|\le c_{1-\alpha}\right\}
\]
holds on both branches.  Define
\[
D_\star=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(\Sigma_{11}(p_\star),\ldots,\Sigma_{dd}(p_\star)\bigr).
\]
The cited joint-convergence and continuous-mapping results therefore show that the studentized vector converges to
\[
Z_\star\sim N(0,R_\star),
\qquad
R_\star=D_\star^{-1/2}\Sigma(p_\star)D_\star^{-1/2},
\]
whose every marginal is standard normal.

Let \(B=\{z:\max_{1\le k\le d}|z_k|\le c_{1-\alpha}\}\).  Its boundary is contained in the finite union of hyperplanes \(\{z:z_k=\pm c_{1-\alpha}\}\).  Each has \(Z_\star\)-probability zero because the corresponding marginal is a continuous standard normal law.  The continuity-set clause of the cited portmanteau lemma thus gives
\[
P_{p_n}\{\mathbf F(p_n)\in\widehat C_{1-\alpha}\}
\longrightarrow P\{Z_\star\in B\}.
\]
Finally, by the union bound and the definition \(c_{1-\alpha}=\Phi^{-1}\{1-\alpha/(2d)\}\),
\[
P\{Z_\star\notin B\}
\le\sum_{k=1}^{d}P\{|Z_{\star,k}|>c_{1-\alpha}\}
=d\,\frac{\alpha}{d}=\alpha.
\]
Thus the limiting coverage along the allegedly bad subsequence is at least \(1-\alpha\), a contradiction.

For every \(n\), the EXT-ID soundness conclusion in the source-specific proposition gives \(\boldsymbol\psi(M_n)=\mathbf F(p_n)\).  The coverage event therefore does not vary with the choice of \(M_n\) inside its exact observed-data fiber.  Taking the infimum over such models and reversing the contradiction argument proves
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{(q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal K}
\inf_{M\in\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)}
P_{q_S,q_0}\{\boldsymbol\psi(M)\in\widehat C_{1-\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]

statements.statement: For the binary specialization \(V=\{W_\star,A_\star,Y_\star\}\), \(\mathcal G=\mathcal G_\star\), \(X=\{A_\star\}\), \(Y=\{Y_\star\}\), and \(T_0=\{W_\star\}\), the answer to the interior gate is affirmative.  In particular, for \(x=1\), \(y=1\), \(\epsilon=1/16\), the uniform tables \(q_S(w,a,y)=1/8\) and \(q_0(w)=1/2\) form a compatible input at which \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}\) returns \(\operatorname{FAIL}\).  There is a compatible represented baseline \((M,\mathcal R,U_0)\in\mathfrak R_{\epsilon,1/4}^{\circ}(\mathcal G_\star,T_0;q_S,q_0)\) and an active direction \(\beta\in\Gamma_{(M,\mathcal R,U_0)}^\perp\) such that \(\beta^{\mathsf T}h_{1,1}=1\).  The perturbations with \(\tau=1/8\) give two models in the same exact fiber with \(P(Y_\star=1\mid\operatorname{do}(A_\star=1))=5/8\) and \(3/8\), respectively.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(U_W\) and \(U_A\) be independent fair binary coordinates and let \(U_0\) be independent of them, with state space \(\mathcal J_0=\{1,2,3,4\}\) and baseline masses \(u_j=1/4\).  Define the recursive structural functions
\[
 W_\star=U_W,
 \qquad A_\star=U_A,
\]
and define the \(Y_\star\)-response indexed by \(U_0=j\) by
\[
 f_{Y_\star}(a,j)=
 \begin{cases}
 0,&j=1,\\
 1,&j=2,\\
 a,&j=3,\\
 1-a,&j=4.
 \end{cases}
\]
Define the selection response by \(f_S(w,y,j)=1\) for \(j\in\{1,2\}\) and \(f_S(w,y,j)=0\) for \(j\in\{3,4\}\).  Each structural function uses only a subset of its displayed parents in \(\mathcal G_\star\), and the only shared exogenous coordinate, \(U_0\), is shared by \(Y_\star\) and \(S\).  Hence this is a recursive semi-Markovian SCM compatible with \(\mathcal G_\star\).  Its exogenous coordinates are independent, their declared state spaces equal their positive supports, and every atom has mass at least \(1/4\).

Selection occurs exactly for types \(1,2\), so \(P_M(S=1)=1/2\).  Conditional on selection, \(W_\star\) and \(A_\star\) remain independent fair coins, while \(Y_\star=0\) and \(Y_\star=1\) each have conditional probability \(1/2\).  Therefore
\[
 q_S(w,a,y)=\frac18\quad\text{for all }(w,a,y)\in\{0,1\}^3,
 \qquad q_0(w)=\frac12.
\]
Thus the input belongs to \(\mathcal C_{1/16}(\mathcal G_\star,T_0)\), and the baseline triple belongs to \(\mathfrak R_{1/16,1/4}^{\circ}\) for that input.

Order the active types as above and put \(\beta=(0,0,1,-1)^{\mathsf T}\).  Integrating over the two fair observed-variable coordinates gives
\[
 a_+=(1,1,0,0)^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad b_0=b_1=\tfrac12\mathbf 1.
\]
For a selected full cell with \(y=0\), \(a_v=(1/4,0,0,0)^{\mathsf T}\); for one with \(y=1\), \(a_v=(0,1/4,0,0)^{\mathsf T}\).  Since \(u^{\mathsf T}a_+=1/2\) and \(u^{\mathsf T}a_v=1/16\), every selected cross-product row is a scalar multiple of \((1,-1,0,0)^{\mathsf T}\).  Consequently \(\beta\) is orthogonal to \(\mathbf 1\), every \(b_t\), and every selected cross-product row, so
\[
 \beta\in\Gamma_{(M,\mathcal R,U_0)}^\perp.
\]
For the cell \((x,y)=(1,1)\), the intervention-response row is
\[
 h_{1,1}=(0,1,1,0)^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad \beta^{\mathsf T}h_{1,1}=1.
\]
Thus \(h_{1,1}\notin\Gamma_{(M,\mathcal R,U_0)}\).

Taking \(\tau=1/8=(1/4)/(2\lVert\beta\rVert_\infty)\), Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}projective\text{-}nullspace\text{-}certificate}\) applies.  More explicitly, the two \(U_0\)-mass vectors are
\[
 u^+=(1/4,1/4,3/8,1/8),
 \qquad u^-=(1/4,1/4,1/8,3/8).
\]
Their selected joint laws and \(W_\star\)-margins remain the displayed \(q_S,q_0\), while
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{M_1}(Y_\star=1\mid\operatorname{do}(A_\star=1))
 &=u^+_2+u^+_3=\frac58,\\
 P_{M_2}(Y_\star=1\mid\operatorname{do}(A_\star=1))
 &=u^-_2+u^-_3=\frac38.
 \end{aligned}
\]
If \(\operatorname{EXT\text{-}ID}\) returned an arithmetic functional at this input, Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}extid\text{-}sound\text{-}termination}\) would force that single functional to equal both \(5/8\) and \(3/8\), a contradiction.  Termination leaves \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) as the only remaining output.  This proves the affirmative gate and its fully interior exact-fiber witness.
