tldr: The project seeks a terminating cell-indexed recovery procedure for \(\psi_{x,y}(M)=P_M(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))\) from the selected conditional \(q_S=P(V\mid S=1)\) and one independently sampled unbiased margin \(q_0=P(T_0)\). The admissible input domain \(\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\) is exactly the image of positive graph-compatible models under \(\operatorname{Obs}_{T_0}(M)=(P_M(V\mid S=1),P_M(T_0))\), and every identification or failure claim is evaluated on the exact fiber over the supplied pair. Each cell run uses a finite graph-indexed inventory and returns \(F_{x,y}\) or \(\operatorname{FAIL}\); the full table is the finite collection of all runs. At \(T_0=\varnothing\), margin extension disappears but graphically licensed population storage remains. The focal question asks whether every failed compatible input admits its own common positive response-atom slack and an active-support projective hedge whose baseline and paired witnesses all reproduce that input exactly. The named three-node fiber is the first executable gate, and the remaining three-node audit uses parameterized real-closed-field elimination and cylindrical algebraic decomposition over symbolic \(q_S,q_0,\epsilon\), never enumeration of observed tables. Complete EXT-ID is only the integration corollary after those gates and the universal hedge are proved. Finite-table inference remains supporting material.

project_justification.gap: Correa, Tian, and Bareinboim define the exact two-law problem and prove IDSB sound but leave completeness unclear. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen can express both sources in do-search, but their Theorem 3 negative-answer guarantee covers Table 1 Rows 1--4 and 6 rather than generalized identifiability in Row 8, whose completeness is listed as unknown. Qiu et al. give a probability-class iff for scalar ATE with an unbiased covariate margin, not arbitrary finite-state semi-Markovian ADMG queries.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a graph-compatible necessity certificate on the realizable two-law image that keeps its represented baseline and both perturbations in one exact fiber while preserving a normalized selected conditional and an independently fixed population margin.
project_justification.fill: The project defines the model-induced observation map, its exact compatible image, and each observed-data fiber; gives an exact source-tagged transition relation over a bounded graph-indexed inventory; and supplies a representation-indexed projective obstruction whose coordinates are exactly the chosen response variable's positive support and whose perturbation has a valid input-specific interior bound. A named three-node exact-fiber witness is the first gate; a parameterized real-closed-field elimination and cylindrical-algebraic partition over symbolic observed tables is the second; and the universal margin-anchored hedge is the focal open theorem. Completeness is only the integration corollary after these ordered gates are discharged.

related_work: Correa, Tian, and Bareinboim (2019, Definition 4, Algorithms 2--3, Theorem 4, and printed pages 2749--2750) give the exact selected-conditional-plus-margin input and sound IDSB recursion while leaving completeness with external data unresolved. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen (2021, Section 2.1, Table 1 at printed page 4, Algorithm 2, and Theorems 2--3) allow inputs of the form \(P(A_i\mid\operatorname{do}(B_i),C_i)\), so they can encode both \(P(V\mid S=1)\) and \(P(T_0)\). Their Theorem 2 proves soundness and termination. Their Theorem 3 at printed page 17, Section 3.4, states that a negative answer implies nonidentifiability for Table 1 Rows 1--4 and 6; Row 8 is generalized identifiability and Table 1 lists its completeness as unknown. The present source pair is a Row 8 instance unless it reduces to one of the covered rows, so the do-search result informs formula discovery but does not settle failure completeness for this exact pair. Qiu et al. (2026, arXiv:2605.13430v3, Definition 2.2, Condition 1, Theorem 3.1, Appendix B.2 Condition 2, and Theorem B.5) characterize full-population scalar ATE identification over classes of propensity scores, covariate-outcome laws, and selection laws. Their external-data theorem has the same selected-law-plus-unbiased-covariate input on the special boundary \(T_0\) equal to the covariate block, but assumes unconfoundedness and overlap, targets only ATE, and includes continuous probability-class examples. It does not decide the arbitrary scalar cells or finite full-table collection here; conversely, the present graph-only model neither implies their probability-class restrictions nor contains their continuous-law examples. Shpitser and Pearl (2006, Theorems 4--6) prove ordinary ID completeness by one-law hedge witnesses. Kivva et al. (2022, Theorem 1 and pages 1027--1030) prove positive gID completeness using latent-law perturbations for unnormalized sources; that method informs the representation-indexed certificate but does not settle the projective two-law fiber. Richardson et al. (2023, Definition 19 and Proposition 25) supply graphical fixing identities used in successful population branches. Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser (2024, Theorems 4--6 and conclusion) study a different systematic-selection likelihood and conjecture completeness there. Duarte et al. (2024, Propositions 1--2 and Theorem 1) provide response-function polynomial machinery for the first named three-node cell gate and the subsequent parameterized semialgebraic audit. Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (2022, Theorems 8, 12, and 14) inform graphical influence-function compilation, while the simultaneous all-cell two-table limit result is only the saturated multinomial delta method. Li, Buchanan, and Cole (2022, equation (3.9) and Propositions 1--2) supply the ACTG 320 benchmark using richer individual-level target covariates.
technical_internal_limitation: The projective theorem is conditional on a fixed graph-compatible response representation and chosen exogenous coordinate; it does not identify a representation from the observed laws. Every response-coordinate state space is defined as its exact positive support, so the perturbation cannot use a zero-mass label. For the named graph \(\mathcal G_\star\), the parameterized audit must certify at least one compatible symbolic input with an EXT-ID terminal cell failure, a represented baseline in that input's exact fiber, and one common positive response-atom slack. Failure of that gate stops the completeness route. The parameterized exact three-node audit and the universal existence, separately for each failed compatible input, of a separating represented baseline are unresolved. Presolve examples remain diagnostics only, including the front-door-type value \(19/36\) and the positive two-node \(A\to Y\to S\) pair with intervention values \(1/3\) and \(2/3\).
honest_scope: Termination holds for every syntactically valid cell input. Soundness, storage validity, boundary reductions, and every failure-completeness claim are restricted to \((q_S,q_0)\in\mathcal C_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0)\), the exact image of \(\mathfrak M_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G)\), and compare models only within \(\mathfrak F_{\epsilon}(\mathcal G,T_0;q_S,q_0)\). In the empty-margin boundary, only margin extension vanishes: population storage and its downstream population closure remain available under the existing graphical predicate. Response representations contain only positive-support atom coordinates, and the common atom slack may depend on the failed compatible input. The focal field-level object is the universal exact-fiber margin-anchored projective hedge. It is pursued only after the named three-node interior fiber failure and a parameterized three-node real-closed-field audit over symbolic \(q_S,q_0,\epsilon\) succeed; no exhaustive observed-table enumeration is claimed. Complete EXT-ID is the resulting integration corollary, not an unconditional headline. The two-source delta method and Bonferroni region are supporting finite-table results. Do-search lacks a failure-completeness theorem for unrestricted Row 8, and Qiu et al.'s iff theorem applies on a probability-class scalar-ATE boundary. The ACTG 320 generalization using WIHS or CNICS margins is a downstream audit consumer, not evidence for the theorem.
